CAPTIONS

CASE FILE 001
On 15 August 1971, the US dollar stopped being redeemable in gold. It was called temporary. It was never reversed.
Everything you earn since then is measured with a ruler that nobody fixed in place.

reel1.text:
REEL 1 SCRIPT · 20 s · The night the anchor was cut

0-2 s · Cover frame. On screen: CASE FILE 001. Sound: paper slide, low hum.
2-6 s · Old TV static, a 1971 calendar page flips to 15 AUGUST. Text: Sunday night. One TV address.
6-10 s · A gold bar on a desk, a chain to a dollar note snaps. Text: The dollar's link to gold was cut.
10-14 s · Stamp hits paper: TEMPORARY. Pause. Second stamp across it: NEVER REVERSED.
14-18 s · Ruler on a desk, slowly shortening. Text: Since then, your money has had no fixed ruler.
18-20 s · Black. Text: Escape the Matrix. The file opens soon.

VO (optional, calm): One Sunday night in 1971, money lost its anchor. It was called temporary. Look how long temporary has lasted.
Use archival-style footage only from sources you have rights to, or generate it in the Veo 3 pipeline.

reel2.text:
REEL 2 SCRIPT · 18 s · Your money has a ruler

0-2 s · Hook text on cover: YOUR MONEY HAS A RULER.
2-6 s · Hand measures a loaf of bread with a ruler marked in rupees. Text: You measure everything in money.
6-10 s · The ruler's marks squeeze closer together. Text: But the ruler itself keeps shrinking.
10-14 s · Same bread, a gold-marked ruler beside it that stays still. Text: Gold is the ruler we use to check.
14-18 s · Text: Not a promise. A measurement. Escape the Matrix. Soon.

No price claims on screen. If you add a number, add its source in the caption.
